title: India Electric Two-Wheeler Market Outlook to 2030
meta_description: Market size, segmentation and competition in India's electric two-wheeler market, covering electric scooters and electric motorcycles.
body_html:
India Electric Two-Wheeler Market Outlook to 2030

Market overview

India is the largest market for electric two-wheelers in the world by unit volume, and electric scooters now account for a meaningful share of new two-wheeler registrations in the major metropolitan areas, according to national vehicle registration statistics. Falling battery pack prices, rising petrol costs and state-level purchase incentives have shifted the economics of daily commuting in favour of electric scooters, especially for delivery fleets and first-time buyers in tier-1 cities.

Demand drivers in the electric two-wheeler market

Total cost of ownership is the decisive purchase factor. An electric scooter covering 40 kilometres a day recovers its price premium in under three years, and the gap widens for gig-economy riders who cover far longer distances. Demand subsidies under the FAME scheme lowered entry prices during the early adoption phase, and several states added registration fee waivers on top.

The availability of public charging infrastructure remains uneven outside the largest cities, which keeps most owners dependent on home charging. Battery swapping is emerging as an alternative for commercial riders: swap stations at fuel retail sites and convenience stores let a rider exchange a depleted pack in under two minutes.

Competitive landscape

The electric two-wheeler market is fragmented. Start-ups that designed electric scooters from the ground up compete with incumbent motorcycle makers that are converting existing platforms. Voltara Motors has built a dealer network across southern and western India and launched an electric motorcycle aimed at rural buyers. Most manufacturers still import lithium-ion battery cells, which leaves margins exposed to currency and commodity swings.

Outlook for electric scooters and motorcycles

We expect electric two-wheelers to exceed a quarter of new two-wheeler sales in India by 2030. Localisation of cell production, better financing for first-time buyers and a denser charging network are the three variables that will decide whether adoption follows the upper or the lower forecast scenario.

Segmentation covers electric scooters, electric motorcycles, low-speed and high-speed models, personal and fleet buyers. It profiles leading participants, reviews regulation and identifies the investment themes that matter most for new entrants.

title: India Electric Vehicle Market Report 2025-2030

body_html:
India Electric Vehicle Market Report 2025-2030

Electric vehicle market overview

India's electric vehicle market has moved from pilot volumes to mainstream adoption in less than a decade. Electric cars remain a small share of passenger vehicle sales, but electric three-wheelers and two-wheeler fleets have already reached commercial scale, and electric buses are being procured by state transport undertakings under gross-cost contracts.

Policy and incentives for electric vehicles

Central demand incentives, production-linked incentives for advanced chemistry cells and a reduced goods and services tax rate on electric vehicles form the core of India's policy support. The FAME scheme has been the most visible instrument for buyers. State EV policies add road-tax exemptions and targets for electric mobility in public fleets.

Policy uncertainty is the main risk flagged by manufacturers. Each revision of subsidy levels has produced a visible dip in monthly sales, followed by a recovery as prices settle.

Passenger electric cars

Electric cars are concentrated in the compact SUV segment, where Voltara Motors and two incumbent carmakers account for most volume. Buyers cite range anxiety and resale value as the main barriers. Public charging infrastructure along intercity highways is expanding, but home and workplace charging still carries most of the load.

Supply chain

Battery packs represent 35 to 40 percent of the cost of an electric vehicle. Domestic cell production is only beginning, so most packs are assembled locally from imported lithium-ion battery cells. Auto parts suppliers that built their business on engines and transmissions are retooling for motors, controllers and thermal management systems.

Outlook

We forecast electric vehicles to reach 15 to 18 percent of total vehicle sales in India by 2030, led by three-wheelers and fleets. The EV market will remain policy-sensitive until battery costs fall far enough for unsubsidised price parity in the passenger segment.

Indonesia EV Charging Infrastructure Market Analysis

EV charging market overview

Indonesia's EV charging infrastructure is at an early stage. Public charging stations are concentrated in Greater Jakarta, Bali and along the Trans-Java toll road, and the state electricity company operates the largest network. Private charge point operators are entering through partnerships with shopping malls, hotels and fuel retailers.

Charging stations and fast chargers

Most installed charge points are AC units at destinations. DC fast charging is limited to a few hundred locations, mostly on highways and at dealerships. The government roadmap targets a large increase in public charging stations by 2030, supported by a special electricity tariff regulation for charging operators.

Battery swapping for motorcycles

Indonesia has one of the largest motorcycle fleets in the world, so battery swapping matters more here than in most markets. Swap stations operated by consortia of motorcycle makers and energy companies are being standardised so that one pack fits several brands.

Demand and utilisation of charging stations

Utilisation is the central commercial question for every operator. With electric vehicles still a small share of the car parc, many public chargers see only a few sessions a day. Operators that bundle charging with ride-hailing fleets or electric taxi depots report far higher utilisation.

Nickel processing investments are positioning Indonesia as a battery materials hub, and policymakers see the charging network as the demand-side counterpart of that strategy.

Outlook

We expect the number of public charging stations in Indonesia to grow more than fivefold by 2030. Fast chargers on intercity corridors and swap networks for motorcycles will grow fastest.

India EV Charging Infrastructure Market Outlook

EV charging market overview

India's EV charging infrastructure has grown rapidly from a low base. Public charging stations are clustered in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune and Hyderabad, while captive charging at fleet depots serves electric buses and three-wheelers. Highway corridors between major cities now have fast chargers at regular intervals.

Business models for charging stations

Charge point operators follow three models: asset-light networks that partner with property owners, oil marketing companies adding chargers at fuel stations, and fleet operators building captive depots. Revenue depends on utilisation, electricity tariffs and land costs. Several states have notified a separate electricity tariff category for public charging stations.

Two-wheelers and battery swapping

Because electric two-wheelers dominate EV sales in India, most charging demand is low-power and happens at home. Battery swapping networks serve delivery riders who cannot wait for a recharge, and a draft national swapping policy aims to define interoperability standards.

Grid integration

Clusters of fast chargers can strain local distribution networks. Operators are pairing chargers with battery storage and rooftop solar to manage peak demand charges, a pattern we expect to spread to large depots.

Outlook for charging infrastructure

We expect public charging points in India to grow at more than 30 percent a year through 2030. DC fast charging along highways and captive depots for fleets will absorb most new investment, while the share of charging stations owned by oil marketing companies rises.

body_html:
Vietnam Solar Power Market Report

Solar power market overview

Vietnam added more solar power capacity in two years than most Southeast Asian countries have built in total, after a generous feed-in tariff triggered a wave of utility-scale and rooftop solar projects. The boom left the country with one of the largest solar fleets in the region, concentrated in the central and southern provinces of Ninh Thuan and Binh Thuan.

Grid constraints and curtailment

Transmission build-out did not keep pace with new solar plants, and curtailment rose sharply in high-irradiation provinces. Developers now face a transition from fixed feed-in tariffs to competitive pricing and direct power purchase agreements with large industrial buyers. Pairing solar plants with energy storage is one option grid planners are studying to reduce curtailment.

Rooftop solar and commercial buyers

Rooftop solar on factories and industrial parks is the most active segment today. Export manufacturers want renewable electricity to meet the sourcing requirements of their customers, and the direct power purchase agreement mechanism gives them a route to contract it. Sunvale Energy and several regional developers have built portfolios of rooftop solar systems on industrial estates.

Technology and supply

Almost all photovoltaic modules installed in Vietnam are imported or assembled from imported cells. Module prices have fallen steeply, which improves project economics even as tariffs decline. Next-generation perovskite solar cells are still at the pilot stage and are not expected to affect Vietnamese procurement before 2030.

Outlook

We expect Vietnam's solar power capacity to keep growing, but at a slower and more grid-aware pace. The national power development plan favours rooftop solar for self-consumption and offshore wind for new large-scale capacity.

India Rooftop Solar Market Outlook

Rooftop solar market overview

Rooftop solar is the fastest-growing part of India's solar power market. Commercial and industrial users account for most installed capacity, but a central subsidy programme for households has created a large residential pipeline. Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Karnataka lead installations.

Residential demand

The household subsidy covers a significant part of the cost of a small rooftop solar system, and public sector banks offer collateral-free loans for the balance. Installers report that awareness and net metering approval times, not price, are now the main constraints on residential uptake.

Commercial and industrial rooftop solar

Factories, warehouses and office campuses install rooftop solar to cut daytime electricity bills that are often cross-subsidised and expensive. Open-access rules and net metering caps vary by state, which shapes where developers focus. Sunvale Energy operates one of the larger commercial portfolios under long-term power purchase agreements.

Storage and grid integration

As rooftop solar penetration grows, distribution companies are pushing back against net metering and favour gross metering or time-of-day tariffs. That shift improves the case for pairing rooftop systems with batteries in commercial buildings, which is covered in our India battery energy storage report.

Outlook

We expect rooftop solar capacity in India to more than double by 2030. Residential installations will grow fastest from a low base, while commercial and industrial users will continue to add the most megawatts.

Saudi Arabia Data Center Market Report

Data center market overview

Saudi Arabia is one of the fastest-growing data center markets in the Middle East. Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam host most operational capacity, and announced projects would multiply installed IT load several times over within five years. Data residency rules for government and financial data keep workloads inside the Kingdom.

Hyperscale and colocation

International cloud providers have announced hyperscale regions in Saudi Arabia, often built with local partners. Colocation providers are expanding wholesale capacity for these tenants, while retail colocation serves banks, government agencies and large enterprises.

Power and cooling

Power availability and cooling are the binding constraints. Data center operators negotiate grid connections years in advance and are exploring on-site generation to meet sustainability commitments. Liquid cooling is moving from pilot deployments to new data halls designed for high-density racks.

Investment and policy

The Vision 2030 programme treats digital infrastructure as a strategic sector. Special economic zones offer land and incentives to data center developers, and sovereign investors are co-funding several campuses. Our GCC data center power demand insight discusses the energy implications across the Gulf region.

We expect Saudi Arabia's data center capacity to grow at more than 20 percent a year through 2030, driven by hyperscale cloud regions and AI training clusters. Supply of accelerator hardware is the main risk to that timeline.

UAE Data Center Market Outlook

Data center market overview

The United Arab Emirates is the most mature data center market in the Middle East. Dubai hosts the largest cluster of colocation facilities, while Abu Dhabi is attracting hyperscale and sovereign AI campuses. Strong international connectivity through subsea cables makes the UAE a regional interconnection hub.

Colocation market

Colocation pricing in Dubai remains high by regional standards because of strong enterprise demand and limited ready capacity. Carrier-neutral operators compete with facilities owned by local conglomerates. Enterprises are moving from server rooms to colocation as they modernise their IT estates and migrate to cloud services.

Hyperscale demand

International cloud providers operate regions in both Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and several are adding capacity for AI workloads. Hyperscale campuses require tens of megawatts per building, so developers are securing large land plots with dedicated substations.

Sustainability of data centers

Cooling consumes a large share of data center electricity in the desert climate. Operators are adopting free-air cooling where possible, high-efficiency chillers and clean energy procurement from large solar parks.

Outlook

We expect the UAE to remain the leading data center hub in the Gulf, with Abu Dhabi's AI-focused campuses growing fastest. Competition from Saudi Arabia will intensify as data residency rules push workloads into the Kingdom.

UAE Cold Chain Market Report

Cold chain market overview

The UAE imports most of its food, which makes cold chain capacity critical infrastructure. Cold storage warehouses around Jebel Ali, Dubai South and Khalifa Port serve importers, re-exporters to the wider Gulf region and a fast-growing online grocery sector.

Cold storage capacity

Multi-temperature cold storage facilities with blast freezing, chilled and ambient zones are replacing older single-temperature warehouses. Automation is rising because labour in sub-zero environments is expensive and hard to retain. ColdPath Logistics recently opened an automated cold storage facility in Dubai South.

Reefer transport

Reefer trucks and temperature-controlled vans connect ports, warehouses and retail stores. Rapid grocery delivery platforms have created demand for small chilled dark stores in residential districts, which require a different network design from bulk distribution.

Pharmaceutical cold chain

Vaccines, biologics and insulin require validated temperature-controlled logistics with continuous monitoring. Dubai's free zones host regional distribution centres for pharmaceutical companies, and Good Distribution Practice certification is a prerequisite to serve them.

Outlook

We expect cold chain capacity in the UAE to grow steadily, led by automated multi-temperature cold storage and medicine distribution. Rising refrigeration costs make on-site generation attractive for new builds.

India Cold Chain Market Outlook to 2030

Cold chain market overview

India is one of the world's largest producers of fruit, vegetables and milk, yet a large share of perishable produce is lost between farm and consumer. The cold chain is fragmented: thousands of small cold storage units, most of them built for potatoes, coexist with a handful of modern multi-commodity operators.

Cold storage

Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Gujarat hold most cold storage capacity, much of it single-commodity and ageing. New investment is going into multi-temperature facilities near consumption centres, supported by central subsidies for integrated cold chain projects. Electricity is the largest operating cost, and many operators are adding solar panels to their roofs.

Reefer transport

The reefer truck fleet is small relative to demand and dominated by owner-operators. Organised temperature-controlled logistics providers are growing with contracts from dairy companies, quick-service restaurant chains and online grocers.

Pharmaceutical and vaccine logistics

India's medicine exports and its national immunisation programme depend on reliable temperature-controlled logistics. The lessons of vaccine distribution are discussed in our insight on vaccine cold chains. Drug makers increasingly outsource this work to specialised providers.

Outlook

We expect the India cold chain market to grow at a double-digit rate through 2030 as organised retail, online grocery and medicine exports expand. ColdPath Logistics and other organised players will gain share from unorganised cold storage operators.

India Diagnostics Market Report

Diagnostics market overview

India's diagnostics market is large and fragmented. Standalone pathology labs and hospital-based laboratories still perform most tests, but national diagnostic chains are growing faster than the market by expanding into tier-2 and tier-3 cities through franchised collection centres.

Pathology labs and test menus

Routine tests such as blood counts, lipid profiles and diabetes panels make up the bulk of volumes. Diagnostic labs are expanding test menus into molecular testing, genetic testing and preventive health packages sold directly to consumers online.

Diagnostic chains and consolidation

Organised diagnostic chains benefit from accreditation, hub-and-spoke logistics for samples and brand trust. Private equity investors have backed a series of acquisitions of regional pathology labs, a trend discussed in our insight on diagnostics consolidation.

In-vitro diagnostics and equipment

Most analysers and reagents used in Indian laboratories are imported, though domestic manufacturers are gaining share in rapid tests. Price controls on certain tests and reagents compress margins for smaller diagnostic laboratories.

Outlook

Thailand E-commerce Logistics Market Analysis

E-commerce logistics market overview

Online marketplaces have transformed parcel logistics in Thailand. Daily parcel volumes have multiplied since 2019, and express delivery companies, marketplace-owned logistics arms and postal operators now compete for every shipment. Bangkok and its surrounding provinces account for most volume, but growth is fastest in the provinces.

Last-mile delivery

Last-mile delivery is the most expensive and competitive part of the chain. Price wars among express delivery companies have pushed per-parcel rates down, and several operators have exited or merged. Motorcycle riders still deliver most parcels, though some operators are testing electric vans in Bangkok.

Fulfilment centres and automation

Marketplaces and third-party logistics providers are building fulfilment centres with automated sortation near Bangkok's ring roads. Cash on delivery remains common, which adds reconciliation costs, although digital payments are growing quickly.

Cross-border flows

A large share of goods sold online in Thailand ships from China, which supports cross-border consolidation hubs and bonded warehouses. Thai sellers use the same networks to reach buyers in Vietnam, Malaysia and the Philippines. Our Vietnam e-commerce logistics report covers the neighbouring market.

Outlook

We expect Thailand's e-commerce logistics market to keep growing faster than overall parcel volumes, with consolidation among express delivery companies and more automation in fulfilment centres.

Malaysia Semiconductor Market Report

Semiconductor market overview

Malaysia has been a semiconductor hub for five decades, with Penang, Kedah and Kulim hosting assembly, test and packaging plants for many of the world's largest chipmakers. The country accounts for a significant share of global back-end semiconductor capacity.

Assembly, test and packaging

Back-end operations remain Malaysia's core strength. Investment is shifting to advanced packaging for high-performance computing and vehicle chips, which requires more capital and engineering talent than traditional wire-bond packaging.

Wafer fabrication and chip design

Front-end wafer fabrication is smaller but growing, with power semiconductor and analogue fabs in Kulim and Sarawak. The national semiconductor strategy aims to move up the value chain into integrated circuit design and to train tens of thousands of engineers. Nimbus Semiconductors opened a design centre in Penang to serve customers across Asia Pacific.

Supply-chain diversification

Multinationals diversifying their supply chains away from a single country have chosen Malaysia for new back-end and equipment plants, as discussed in our semiconductor supply chain insight. Demand from new data centers in Johor also creates local customers for server components.

Outlook

Philippines Fintech Market Outlook

Fintech market overview

The Philippines has moved quickly from cash to digital payments. Mobile e-wallets are used by a majority of urban adults, and QR payments at small merchants have become common. Remittances from overseas workers, a large part of household income, are increasingly received in digital wallets.

Digital payments and e-wallets

Two e-wallets dominate consumer payments, with PayLane and smaller challengers competing for merchant acceptance. The central bank's national QR standard allows any wallet to pay at any participating merchant, which lowered acceptance costs for small shops.

Digital lending and neobanks

Digital lending is growing quickly as e-wallets offer buy-now-pay-later and small cash loans based on transaction data. Licensed digital banks, or neobanks, are competing for deposits with high savings rates, but most are not yet profitable.

GCC Energy Storage Market Report

Energy storage market overview

Energy storage in the GCC has moved from pilots to some of the largest battery energy storage projects in the world. Saudi Arabia and the UAE are procuring gigawatt-hours of grid storage to shift daytime generation into the evening peak and stabilise grids as renewables grow.

Solar-plus-storage tenders

Most new capacity is procured through solar-plus-storage tenders, in which developers bid a single tariff for a photovoltaic plant and a co-located battery storage system. Record-low bids have shown that firm daytime and evening supply can compete with gas-fired generation in the Gulf region.

Technology choices for battery storage

Lithium iron phosphate batteries dominate new grid storage projects because of their safety and cycle life in high ambient temperatures. Thermal management is critical: containers must operate reliably at summer temperatures above 45 degrees Celsius. Pumped hydro and long-duration technologies are being studied for later phases.

Project pipeline

Saudi Arabia's procurement programme and the UAE's grid-scale projects account for most of the pipeline, with Oman and Qatar following. Developers source cells mainly from Asian suppliers, and some GCC investors are taking stakes in battery manufacturing abroad to secure supply.

India Lithium-ion Battery Manufacturing Market Outlook

Lithium-ion battery market overview

India's lithium-ion battery demand is growing quickly, driven by electric vehicles, consumer electronics and grid storage, yet almost all battery cells are still imported. A production-linked incentive scheme for advanced chemistry cells has attracted commitments for several gigafactories, the first of which are now commissioning.

Gigafactory investment

Announced gigafactory capacity in India exceeds 100 gigawatt-hours, but execution lags announcements. Corecell Batteries is building one of the first large cell plants in Gujarat, using lithium iron phosphate chemistry for two-wheeler and stationary applications. Joint ventures with Asian cell makers provide technology for most other projects.

Pack assembly

Battery pack assembly is already a domestic industry, with hundreds of assemblers supplying electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers. Safety incidents prompted stricter testing standards for battery packs, which favour larger assemblers with better quality control.

Raw material dependence

India has limited domestic reserves of lithium, nickel and cobalt, so cell makers depend on imported cathode materials and lithium carbonate. Securing supply from Australia, South America and Southeast Asia is a strategic priority, covered in our battery materials report.

Next-generation chemistries

Sodium-ion and solid-state batteries are on the research agenda of several Indian institutes and start-ups, but commercial production is not expected before the end of the decade.

Battery materials market overview

Southeast Asia has become central to the global supply of battery materials. Indonesia holds the world's largest nickel reserves and has used an export ban on raw ore to attract smelters and precursor plants. The Philippines is a major nickel ore exporter, and Thailand and Vietnam host smaller processing projects.

Nickel processing in Indonesia

High-pressure acid leach plants in Sulawesi and the Maluku islands produce mixed hydroxide precipitate, an intermediate for cathode materials. Most processing capacity is financed and operated by Chinese companies in partnership with Indonesian firms, which raises questions about supply-chain diversification for Western buyers. Cathode materials and anode materials

Precursor and cathode materials plants are being built next to nickel smelters to capture more value. Anode materials, mostly graphite, are still imported from outside the region. Several projects aim to produce battery-grade lithium from imported spodumene concentrate.

Coal-fired captive power for smelters, tailings disposal and deforestation are significant environmental risks. Buyers in Europe and North America increasingly require traceability and lower-carbon processing, which may favour projects powered by renewable energy.

Vietnam Wind Power Market Outlook

Wind power market overview

Vietnam's wind power sector grew quickly under a feed-in tariff that rewarded projects commissioned before a deadline, leaving a fleet of onshore wind and nearshore wind farms in the Mekong Delta and the central highlands. The next phase depends on offshore wind, where Vietnam has some of the best resources in Asia.

Onshore and nearshore wind

Onshore wind farms in the central provinces and intertidal nearshore projects along the Mekong Delta coast make up the installed base. Many projects missed the tariff deadline and are negotiating transitional prices with the state power company.

Offshore wind pipeline

The national power development plan targets several gigawatts of offshore wind by the early 2030s. Developers have surveyed sites off the south-central coast, but a legal framework for allocating seabed areas and foreign participation is still being finalised. Grid constraints limit how much new wind power the system can absorb. Grid planners see battery storage and new interconnectors as essential to integrate variable renewables.

Rising demand from supermarkets, quick-service restaurants and online grocers is driving investment in modern facilities.

Cold storage capacity

Port-side cold storage facilities handle imported meat and seafood, while inland facilities serve retailers and food processors. New investment from domestic conglomerates and foreign operators is adding multi-temperature warehouses, and ColdPath Logistics entered through an acquisition near Manila.

Temperature-controlled logistics

The archipelago geography makes temperature-controlled logistics expensive. Reefer containers on inter-island shipping routes and reefer trucks on Luzon form the backbone of the network.

Policy

The government has identified cold chain development as a priority for food security and offers incentives for facilities in agricultural regions.

Outlook

We expect cold chain capacity in the Philippines to grow at a double-digit rate through 2030, led by multi-temperature cold storage near ports and food processing zones.

UAE Diagnostics Market Outlook

Diagnostics market overview

The UAE diagnostics market is served by hospital laboratories, independent diagnostic labs and a growing number of regional chains. Mandatory medical cover for residents of Dubai and Abu Dhabi has expanded access to routine testing, and preventive screening is promoted by public health authorities.

Pathology labs

Reference laboratories in Dubai and Abu Dhabi process specialised tests for hospitals across the Gulf region. Pathology labs are investing in automation and digital pathology to handle rising volumes.

Genomics and specialised testing

National genome programmes and premarital screening create demand for genetic testing. Diagnostic laboratories with molecular capability are expanding into oncology and fertility testing.

Competition

Regional chains compete with international laboratory groups that have entered through joint ventures. Price regulation by payers limits margins on routine tests, pushing labs towards specialised diagnostics.

India Health Insurance Market Report

Health insurance market overview

Health insurance is the largest and fastest-growing segment of India's general insurance market. Group cover provided by employers, retail policies bought by families and a large government-funded scheme for low-income households together cover a growing share of the population.

Retail and group health insurance

Retail health insurance is sold through agents, banks and online aggregators. Standalone health insurers compete with multi-line general insurers, and group policies offered by employers remain the entry point for many urban workers.

Claims and hospital networks

Cashless claims at network hospitals are the main service differentiator. Rising hospital costs and medical inflation have pushed insurers to negotiate package rates and invest in fraud analytics. Outpatient cover, including laboratory tests and consultations, is a growing product category.

Insurtech

Insurtech platforms have simplified policy comparison and purchase, and some insurers now offer products with wellness rewards linked to fitness trackers.

We expect India's health insurance premiums to grow at a mid-to-high teens rate through 2030 as penetration rises in smaller cities.

Qatar Logistics Market Report

Logistics market overview

Ports and freight

Hamad Port handles most container freight, with feeder connections to neighbouring ports. Air freight through Doha's hub airport benefits from the national carrier's cargo network.

Sea-air transshipment, where goods arrive by ship and leave by air, has become a niche strength, and bonded storage lets cargo be re-exported without customs duty. Road freight links to Saudi Arabia now carry growing volumes of construction materials and consumer goods.

Warehousing and free zones

Logistics parks and free zones offer warehousing for re-export, contract logistics and light manufacturing. Occupancy has improved as companies serving the Middle East set up regional distribution in Qatar.

Contract logistics

Bangladesh Pharmaceutical Market Outlook

Pharmaceutical market overview

Bangladesh's pharmaceutical industry meets almost all domestic demand for medicines, a rare achievement among least-developed countries. Generic drugs dominate, and a few large domestic manufacturers account for most sales.

Exports of generic drugs

Exports are small but growing, with manufacturers supplying generic drugs to markets in Asia, Africa and Latin America, and a few plants approved by stringent regulators.

Exporters are building plants that meet the standards of regulators in Europe and North America, which opens larger markets but requires sustained investment in quality systems and documentation. Contract manufacturing for multinational companies is another route to growth.

Active pharmaceutical ingredients

The industry imports most active pharmaceutical ingredients, largely from China and India. A dedicated API industrial park near Dhaka aims to build domestic capacity before trade preferences end.

Graduation from least-developed status

Bangladesh's graduation from least-developed country status will end patent waivers under trade rules, which may raise costs for some medicines. Manufacturers are investing in quality systems and new product registrations to prepare.

title: Battery Swapping for Electric Two-Wheelers in India: Does the Model Work?
meta_description: Why battery swapping is gaining ground with delivery riders in India, and what still holds the model back.
body_html:
Battery Swapping for Electric Two-Wheelers in India: Does the Model Work?

Battery swapping promises to remove the two biggest objections to electric two-wheelers in India: the upfront cost of the battery and the time it takes to recharge. A rider leases the pack instead of buying it, and exchanges it at a swap station in under two minutes.

Battery swapping is not new: it was tried for electric cars more than a decade ago and failed because carmakers would not agree on a common pack. Two-wheelers are a better fit. Packs are light enough to lift by hand, riders are price-sensitive commercial users, and the dense street networks of Indian cities let a single station serve many riders within a short ride. That combination explains why investors have returned to the model.

Who uses swap stations

Delivery riders and two-wheeler taxi drivers are the core users. They cover well over 100 kilometres a day, cannot afford to wait for a charge and value the lower purchase price of an electric scooter sold without a pack. Swap operators report that a busy station in Bengaluru or Delhi serves several hundred swaps a day.

The economics of battery swapping

Operators carry the cost of the battery fleet, which means utilisation decides profitability. Every pack must cycle several times a day to pay back its cost, and a lithium-ion battery that sits on a shelf is dead capital. Operators also need spare packs in the network, so they hold more batteries than vehicles on the road.

Our India electric two-wheeler market report estimates that fleets using swapping could account for a significant share of commercial electric two-wheeler sales by 2030.

Interoperability is the open question

Today most swap networks serve one vehicle brand, which limits network effects. A national battery swapping policy proposes common standards for pack dimensions, connectors and data sharing. Manufacturers that design their own packs resist standardisation, while swap operators argue that shared stations are the only way to reach scale.

What to watch

Three signals will show whether battery swapping becomes mainstream: the final interoperability standard, the cost of financing large battery fleets and the density of public charging stations, which competes for the same riders.

title: Why Charging Infrastructure Lags EV Sales in Southeast Asia
meta_description: Charging stations in Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and Malaysia are not keeping pace with electric vehicle sales. We look at why.
body_html:
Why Charging Infrastructure Lags EV Sales in Southeast Asia

Electric vehicle sales in Southeast Asia have grown far faster than the charging infrastructure meant to support them. In Thailand, the region's largest EV market, the number of electric cars per public charging station has risen every year since subsidies began.

The gap matters because surveys of prospective buyers in the region consistently rank access to charging as a top concern, alongside price. Carmakers that sell electric vehicles in Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia now bundle home chargers with new cars and fund their own fast chargers at dealerships, an expensive stopgap that shows how far public networks lag behind demand. Governments have set targets for public chargers, but most are behind schedule.

A utilisation trap

Charge point operators face a familiar problem: utilisation is too low to pay for new charging stations until more EVs are on the road, and buyers hesitate until the network is denser. Operators in Indonesia report that many public chargers see only a few sessions a day, as our Indonesia EV charging report shows.

Grid connections and tariffs

DC fast charging hubs need grid connections that take months or years to approve. Electricity tariffs for charging operators vary widely across the region: Indonesia and Thailand have special tariffs, while Vietnam and Malaysia are still developing them.

Two-wheelers change the picture

Motorcycles dominate road transport in Indonesia and Vietnam, and their riders mostly charge at home or use battery swapping. Public charging infrastructure planning based on car ownership alone misses the largest group of electric vehicle users in these markets.

What would close the gap

Fleet depots, highway fast chargers funded by carmakers, and clear tariffs for charging operators would do more than subsidies for individual charging stations. We expect the gap to narrow after 2027 as utilisation improves along the busiest corridors.

title: Perovskite Solar Cells: How Close Is Commercialisation?
meta_description: Perovskite and tandem solar cells promise higher efficiency than silicon. We assess the path to commercial photovoltaic modules.
body_html:
Perovskite Solar Cells: How Close Is Commercialisation?

Perovskite solar cells have moved from laboratory curiosity to pilot production lines in less than fifteen years. Tandem cells that stack a perovskite layer on top of silicon have reached record efficiencies, and several manufacturers worldwide plan commercial photovoltaic modules within the next few years.

Conventional crystalline silicon cells are approaching their practical efficiency limit, so the industry is looking for the next step. Perovskites are a family of crystal structures that absorb sunlight strongly and can be tuned to capture parts of the spectrum that silicon uses poorly. Combined with silicon in a tandem cell, they offer a route to efficiencies well above what silicon can reach alone, without abandoning existing factories and supply chains.

Why perovskite matters for solar power

Efficiency gains reduce the area, glass and mounting needed per watt, which lowers the cost of solar power even when module prices are already low. Perovskite layers can be deposited at low temperatures, which could make manufacturing cheaper than for conventional cells.

Durability is the barrier

Perovskite materials degrade when exposed to moisture, heat and ultraviolet light. Bankable solar panels need warranties of 25 to 30 years, and outdoor field data for perovskite modules covers only a few years. Encapsulation and new compositions are improving stability, but certification bodies and lenders remain cautious.

Who is investing

Sunvale Energy has announced a pilot line for tandem modules, and research consortia have published field test results from installations in hot climates. Hot, humid markets such as Vietnam and the Gulf are where durability will be tested hardest.

Outlook

We expect the first commercial tandem modules to reach rooftop solar customers before utility-scale projects, where lenders demand long operating records. Mainstream adoption is unlikely before the early 2030s.

title: GCC Data Center Boom: What It Means for Power Demand
meta_description: Hyperscale data centers in Saudi Arabia and the UAE will add gigawatts of new electricity demand. We look at how the Gulf will supply it.
body_html:
GCC Data Center Boom: What It Means for Power Demand

Announced data center projects in the GCC add up to several gigawatts of IT load, most of it in Saudi Arabia and the UAE. If even half are built, data centers will become one of the fastest-growing sources of electricity demand in the Gulf region.

Gulf governments see data centers as a pillar of economic diversification, and sovereign investors are funding AI campuses alongside international cloud providers. Cheap land and abundant capital make the region attractive, but power is the resource that will decide how much of the announced pipeline is built, and how quickly. The answer will also shape tariff design, because large campuses negotiate terms that other industrial customers do not receive.

Hyperscale campuses need firm power

Hyperscale and AI campuses run around the clock and need firm, high-quality power. Developers are signing long-term supply agreements with grid operators and exploring dedicated generation on site. Our UAE data center report describes how Abu Dhabi campuses are securing land with dedicated substations.

Clean power commitments

Cloud providers have committed to match their consumption with clean electricity. In the Gulf that means contracts with large solar power plants, increasingly paired with energy storage to cover night-time load. Cooling adds to demand: in summer it can account for a large share of a data center's consumption.

Grid planning implications

Grid planners in Saudi Arabia and the UAE are revising demand forecasts to include data centers explicitly. Concentrated demand near Riyadh, Dammam, Dubai and Abu Dhabi will require new transmission lines and substations.

Outlook

We expect data centers to account for a mid-single-digit share of electricity demand in the leading Gulf markets by 2030, up from a negligible share today.

title: Lessons from Vaccine Distribution for India's Cold Chain
meta_description: What India's vaccine programmes reveal about temperature-controlled logistics, and how the cold chain for medicines is changing.
body_html:
Lessons from Vaccine Distribution for India's Cold Chain

Vaccine distribution is the most demanding test of a cold chain. India's national immunisation programme moves hundreds of millions of doses a year through a network of cold storage points that reaches remote villages, and it has become a reference for temperature-controlled logistics across the country.

During the pandemic the network was stretched to deliver new vaccines that required colder storage than routine immunisations. Ultra-low temperature freezers were installed at regional stores, cold boxes were redesigned for longer journeys, and district officials learned to plan deliveries around power outages. Many of those investments remain in place and now support routine programmes, while private operators have hired staff trained during the campaign.

Monitoring the last mile

Electronic temperature loggers and a digital stock management system let programme managers see the temperature and stock of every cold storage point in near real time. The same approach is now being adopted by commercial cold chain operators that serve pharmaceutical companies.

Commercial pharmaceutical logistics

Pharmaceutical exporters need validated temperature-controlled logistics from factory to port. Specialised providers such as ColdPath Logistics operate GDP-certified cold storage near manufacturing clusters in Gujarat, Telangana and Maharashtra. Our India pharmaceutical market report covers the export side.

Gaps that remain

Reefer transport is still the weakest link. Most refrigerated trucks belong to small owner-operators without real-time monitoring, and power cuts in rural areas threaten cold storage points without backup.

Outlook

We expect the share of medicines moving through organised, monitored cold chain networks in India to rise steadily as export quality requirements tighten.

title: What Southeast Asia Can Learn from India's Digital Payments Model
meta_description: India's Unified Payments Interface transformed digital payments. We compare it with fintech markets in the Philippines and Indonesia.
body_html:
What Southeast Asia Can Learn from India's Digital Payments Model

India's Unified Payments Interface processes more real-time digital payments than any other system in the world. Its design, an interoperable public rail on which banks and fintech apps compete, is being studied by regulators across Southeast Asia.

The comparison is not straightforward. India built its system on a national digital identity programme and a banking push that opened hundreds of millions of accounts, while the Philippines and Indonesia rely more on e-wallets run by private companies. Remittances, cash habits and the role of wallets backed by mobile operators differ too. Still, the core lesson, that a shared public payment rail lowers costs for everyone, applies across the region.

Interoperability first

UPI lets any app pay any bank account using a simple identifier, so merchants accept one QR code for every wallet. In the Philippines and Indonesia, national QR standards are moving in the same direction, but e-wallets still compete partly by locking in merchants. Our Philippines fintech report describes the QR standard in detail.

Zero fees and who pays

Person-to-person and small merchant payments on UPI carry no fees, which drove adoption but leaves payment apps without direct revenue. Fintech firms such as PayLane monetise through digital lending, insurance distribution and merchant services instead.

Cross-border links

Linkages between India's system and real-time payment systems in Singapore and other countries allow instant remittances. Similar links within ASEAN would cut remittance costs for migrant workers.

Outlook

We expect at least two more Southeast Asian countries to adopt fully interoperable real-time retail payment systems by 2028.

title: The Economics of Last-Mile Delivery in Thailand and Vietnam
meta_description: Parcel prices, rider costs and density: why last-mile delivery margins are so thin in Thailand and Vietnam.
body_html:
The Economics of Last-Mile Delivery in Thailand and Vietnam

Last-mile delivery accounts for roughly half of the cost of shipping a parcel in Thailand and Vietnam. Price wars among express delivery companies have pushed per-parcel revenue down faster than costs, and several operators have exited.

The squeeze has come from both sides. Marketplaces negotiate low rates because they control huge volumes, and consumers have come to expect free shipping on almost every order. At the same time, rider wages, fuel and vehicle costs have risen, and failed deliveries, which require a second attempt or a return to the seller, add cost that is rarely priced in. Operators that survive will be those that raise productivity per rider.

Density decides margins

A rider who delivers 120 parcels a day in central Bangkok earns the operator a margin; the same rider in a provincial town delivering 40 does not. Operators are redesigning routes, pooling volumes and adding parcel lockers to raise drops per hour.

Marketplaces take control

Large marketplaces route a growing share of their parcels through their own logistics arms and fulfilment centres, leaving independent express delivery companies with lower-density volume. Our Thailand e-commerce logistics report quantifies this shift.

Vietnam's motorbike model

In Vietnam, motorbike couriers navigate narrow alleys that vans cannot enter, which keeps fleet costs low but limits parcel size. Express delivery operators in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City are investing in sortation hubs to cut handling time.

Outlook

We expect further consolidation among last-mile delivery operators in both countries, with survivors competing on reliability and returns handling rather than price.

title: Indonesia's Nickel Bet: Building a Battery Materials Industry
meta_description: How Indonesia's ore export ban created a battery materials processing industry, and the risks that come with it.
body_html:
Indonesia's Nickel Bet: Building a Battery Materials Industry

Indonesia banned exports of raw nickel ore to force processing at home. A decade later the country produces a large share of the world's refined nickel and is moving into precursor and cathode materials for batteries.

The strategy is one of the most ambitious examples of resource nationalism in recent years. It has brought tens of billions of dollars of investment into processing, created industrial towns on islands that had little industry before, and turned nickel into one of the country's largest exports by value. It has also drawn trade disputes, as well as criticism over deforestation, air pollution and working conditions at some of the industrial parks.

From ore to cathode materials

Smelters in Sulawesi and the Maluku islands produce nickel pig iron for steel and, increasingly, mixed hydroxide precipitate for battery materials. Precursor plants built alongside them are the first step towards domestic cathode materials production. Our Southeast Asia battery materials report maps the projects.

Investment and ownership

Chinese companies finance and operate most processing capacity, often in industrial parks with captive coal power. Western buyers seeking supply chains outside China face a dilemma: Indonesian nickel is abundant, but its ownership and carbon footprint complicate sourcing rules.

Downstream ambitions

Indonesia wants to go further, into battery cells and electric vehicles. Local content rules for electric motorcycles and cars aim to create domestic demand for batteries made from Indonesian nickel.

Outlook

We expect Indonesia to remain the largest source of nickel for batteries through 2030, while the share of lower-carbon processing rises slowly.

title: How the Semiconductor Supply Chain Shift Is Reshaping Malaysia
meta_description: Chipmakers diversifying their supply chains are investing in Malaysia, Vietnam and India. Malaysia is the biggest winner so far.
body_html:
How the Semiconductor Supply Chain Shift Is Reshaping Malaysia

Semiconductor companies are spreading production across more countries to reduce geopolitical risk. Malaysia, with fifty years of experience in assembly and test, has captured a large share of the new back-end investment.

The shift began with trade tensions and accelerated after supply shortages during the pandemic exposed how concentrated chip production had become. Customers now ask suppliers to show that they can produce in more than one country, and governments across Asia compete with incentives, industrial land and training programmes. For Malaysia, the challenge is to turn this wave of investment into higher-value activities rather than more of the same assembly work.

Back-end expansion

Chipmakers are expanding assembly, test and advanced packaging plants in Penang and Kedah. Equipment suppliers have followed, building plants that serve fabs across Asia. Nimbus Semiconductors doubled its Penang workforce in two years.

Competition from Vietnam and India

Vietnam is attracting assembly and test investment with lower labour costs, and India offers large subsidies for its first wafer fabrication plants. Malaysia's advantage is its ecosystem of suppliers and experienced engineers, but talent shortages are a constraint.

Moving up the value chain

Malaysia's national semiconductor strategy aims to grow chip design and front-end manufacturing. See our Malaysia semiconductor market report for capacity and investment data.

Outlook

We expect Malaysia to keep its lead in back-end semiconductor manufacturing in Southeast Asia through 2030, with design capability growing from a small base. Universities in Penang and Kuala Lumpur are expanding engineering courses to meet demand.

title: Why India's Diagnostics Chains Are Consolidating
meta_description: Acquisitions of regional pathology labs are reshaping India's diagnostics market. We explain the drivers.
body_html:
Why India's Diagnostics Chains Are Consolidating

India's largest diagnostic chains have spent the past three years buying regional pathology labs. Consolidation is driven by the economics of scale in laboratory testing and by the arrival of online aggregators that compete on price.

Diagnostics in India has long been a local business, with doctors referring patients to labs they know personally. That model is changing as patients book tests online, compare prices and expect home sample collection. Chains with strong brands, accreditation and digital booking capture this demand, while small labs struggle to invest in automation and quality systems. Private equity has funded much of the consolidation, betting on steady growth in testing volumes.

Scale economics in pathology labs

A central laboratory that runs automated analysers around the clock has far lower cost per test than a small standalone lab. Chains acquire regional diagnostic labs, keep their collection centres and brand, and move processing to regional hubs.

Online aggregators

Online platforms sell discounted test packages and route samples to partner labs. Their pricing pressure has hit standalone diagnostic laboratories hardest and pushed many owners to sell.

What acquirers want

Acquirers value accreditation, a strong local doctor network and a presence in tier-2 cities. Our India diagnostics market report tracks market shares of the leading chains.

Outlook

We expect organised chains to raise their share of India's diagnostics market steadily through 2030, with further acquisitions in the north and east of the country. Smaller labs that remain independent will increasingly join networks or franchise agreements.

Solid-State Batteries: Outlook for Commercial Production

Solid-state batteries replace the liquid electrolyte of a lithium-ion battery with a solid one, promising higher energy density and better safety. Pilot lines are running, but mass production remains years away.

Manufacturing challenges

Producing thin, defect-free solid electrolyte layers at scale is difficult, and interfaces between layers degrade with cycling. Corecell Batteries has a pilot line but has not announced a production date.

title: How the FAME Scheme Shaped Electric Vehicle Adoption in India
meta_description: India's FAME scheme subsidised electric vehicles for nearly a decade. We assess what it achieved and what replaced it.
body_html:
How the FAME Scheme Shaped Electric Vehicle Adoption in India

The FAME scheme was India's main demand incentive for electric vehicles. Across its phases it subsidised buses, three-wheelers, cars and scooters, and it shaped pricing, product design and manufacturer strategy in the Indian EV market.

The scheme's first phase was modest and focused on creating awareness. The second phase, launched with a much larger budget, made demand subsidies conditional on minimum performance and localisation requirements, which forced manufacturers to source more components in India. That design choice made FAME as much an industrial policy as a consumer incentive, and it continues to shape the structure of the Indian supply base for electric vehicles.

What FAME II funded

FAME II concentrated subsidies on vehicles used intensively: electric buses procured by state transport undertakings, three-wheelers and commercial fleets. It also funded public charging stations in cities and on highways, and tied subsidies to localisation of key components.

Effects on electric vehicle prices

Subsidies lowered the price of electric vehicles closer to petrol equivalents. When subsidy levels were cut, prices rose and monthly sales dipped before recovering. Our India electric vehicle market report charts these cycles.

Compliance problems

Investigations found that some manufacturers claimed subsidies without meeting localisation rules, which led to recoveries and tighter audits. The episode made later schemes more cautious about verification.

After FAME

Successor programmes kept support for electric mobility but shifted the emphasis to manufacturing incentives for cells and vehicles. We expect demand subsidies for private electric vehicles to keep shrinking as prices fall.

Contact Our Analysts

How to reach us

Use the form on this page to ask a question about a report, request a free sample or discuss a custom research project. An analyst who covers the relevant market will reply within one working day.

For billing and licence questions, please include your order number so our client services team can find your account quickly. You can also write to our sales team.

Custom research

Our custom research team designs studies around your questions: market entry assessments, competitor benchmarking, customer surveys and due diligence. Tell us about your objectives and timeline, and we will propose a scope and a quote. Most custom projects take between four and ten weeks, depending on the number of interviews and markets involved.
